# pqtools

> Run, lint and format Power Query M without Power BI. pqtools executes a `.pq`
> query end to end against local CSV files in pure Python (no dependencies), and
> is also a linter, formatter and safe renamer for M source - including the
> queries stored inside `.pbix`, `.pbit` and `.xlsx` files.

Install with `pip install pqtools`. Python 3.11+. MIT. Unofficial; not
affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft.

## What it does

- `pq eval report.pq` - run a query. Local-file sources (`Csv.Document`,
  `File.Contents`, `Text.FromBinary`) run natively, then the whole
  transformation chain: `Table.PromoteHeaders`, `Table.TransformColumnTypes`,
  `Table.SelectRows`, `Table.Group`, all six `JoinKind` values, pivot/unpivot,
  `List.*`, `Text.*`, `Number.*`, and date/time/duration. 353 M builtins.
  Output as JSON or CSV.
- `pq list report.pbix` - name every query inside a .pbix / .pbit / .xlsx.
  Each name is usable directly as `pq eval FILE --member NAME`.
- `pq eval report.pbix --member Sales` - run one query out of a container,
  including the inline "Enter Data" tables Power BI embeds as a base64
  deflate payload.
- `pq check report.pq` - lint, with CI-shaped exit codes.
- `pq format report.pq` - format, via Microsoft's own pinned
  `@microsoft/powerquery-formatter`.
- `pq rename report.pq --from Old --to New` - rename a `let` binding without a
  find-and-replace hitting a matching string literal.
- Reads `.pbix` / `.pbit` / `.xlsx` containers to analyse the M inside them.
  `pq format` / `pq rename` / `pq replace-source` print the edited M and
  save it with `--write`. `pq add --name N --source '...' --write` adds a
  brand-new query. Any `--write` on a container writes a `<file>.bak` first.

<!-- coverage:start -->
pqtools implements **292 of the 634** functions in Microsoft's Power Query M reference (46%). Every one of the remaining 342 is recognised by name and refuses with a typed error saying which outside system it would need - never a wrong answer, and never the bare "unknown identifier" that a typo produces.
<!-- coverage:end -->

## What it deliberately does NOT do

This matters more than the feature list, because guessing here produces a wrong
answer that looks right.

- It does not fold queries. Power Query rewrites `Table.SelectRows` into a
  `WHERE` clause and makes the remote engine do the work; pqtools fetches and
  filters locally. Results agree; the work happens in a different place, and
  on a large remote table that difference is the whole performance story.
  pandas does not fold either.
- It does not run `SharePoint.*`, which needs a tenant identity there is no
  honest way to stand in for. It raises a typed `M_EVAL_UNSUPPORTED` naming
  itself. `Table.Fuzzy*` is refused the same way: the similarity algorithm is
  not documented precisely enough to reproduce, and an approximate join
  returns wrong rows rather than an error.
- Connectors that ARE implemented - `Web.Contents`, `OData.Feed`,
  `Folder.Files`, `Folder.Contents`, `Excel.Workbook`, `Sql.Database`,
  `PostgreSQL.Database`, `MySQL.Database`, `Oracle.Database`, `Odbc.Query`,
  `Odbc.DataSource` - are OFF BY DEFAULT and refuse with `M_IO_BLOCKED`
  naming the flag that would enable them (`--allow-net`, `--allow-db`). The
  query names the destination, and the query is often somebody else's file.
  Even under `--allow-net`, internal and link-local addresses stay blocked
  (169.254.169.254 is the cloud metadata endpoint) unless
  `--allow-private-net` is also passed.
- It is not a Power Query replacement and does not reimplement the Mashup
  Engine.
- It never approximates. Any construct it cannot evaluate exactly raises a
  typed error naming it, rather than returning a plausible wrong value.
- It carries Microsoft's ENTIRE documented function list (`pqtools.catalog`,
  generated from Microsoft Learn by `scripts/sync_m_catalog.py`). A documented
  function it does not implement refuses with a message saying which outside
  system it would need; a name that is not M at all still reports "unknown
  identifier". Those are different problems with different fixes, so do not
  describe an unimplemented function as "not a Power Query function".
- It does NOT register any name Power Query lacks. `tests/test_catalog.py`
  enforces this against Microsoft's reference, because a function that exists
  here and not in Power Query means a query passes here and fails there -
  worse than a missing function. Two such names shipped by mistake before
  0.10.0 (`Uri.UnescapeDataString`, `Table.SelectDuplicates`) and are removed;
  neither should be reintroduced or recommended.
- Excel itself has never opened a workbook this rewrote (Excel was not
  installed where the write path was validated). The rebuild is verified four
  ways - CRC intact, every member except the DataMashup part byte-identical,
  the M reading back, and openpyxl opening the result to the same sheets and
  values - and every `--write` leaves a `.bak`. Do not describe writing as
  unsafe, and do not describe it as Excel-certified.
- It sends no telemetry, and makes no network call unless the query asks
  for one AND the caller passed `--allow-net` or `--allow-db`.

## Correct usage

Run a query whose source is a local CSV - nothing to supply:

```bash
pq eval report.pq --format csv
```

Run a query whose source needs an engine, or whose path belongs to the machine
that authored it - bind the source step instead:

```bash
pq eval report.pq --bind Source=data.csv
```

From Python (this is the import that works; `evaluate` is exported at the
package root):

```python
from pqtools import evaluate

rows = evaluate(query_text, bindings={"Source": [{"a": 1}]})
```

A table is `list[dict[str, Any]]`. `Csv.Document` does NOT promote headers -
it returns `Column1..ColumnN`, and `Table.PromoteHeaders` is a separate step,
exactly as in Power Query.
